skill.name: skill-creator
skill.description: Create, revise, evaluate, benchmark, optimize, and package AI skills through a structured workflow with realistic tests and human review.
skill.summary: Build and improve AI skills with repeatable evaluation, review, optimization, and packaging workflows.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most scanner alerts are Markdown, CSS, loopback, or key-name false positives. Confirmed risks include unsafe HTML embedding, untrusted content sent to Claude CLI, occupied-port process termination, external asset requests, and symlink-following file collection. Publication should wait until the high-impact paths are hardened.

remediation.issue: Untrusted data is inserted into script and innerHTML contexts.
remediation.suggestion: Use non-executable JSON script blocks, escape closing script sequences, validate data types, and build browser content with textContent or sanitized DOM APIs.

remediation.issue: The optimizer sends untrusted skill and eval content to a local Claude process.
remediation.suggestion: Treat embedded content as data, disable tools for optimization calls, use a restricted environment, and pass only required authentication variables.

remediation.issue: The viewer terminates every process using the requested port.
remediation.suggestion: Never kill unrelated processes automatically. Detect conflicts and choose an available port, or require explicit user confirmation before termination.

remediation.issue: Packaging and viewer discovery follow symlinks outside their selected roots.
remediation.suggestion: Reject symlinks and verify every resolved path remains under the skill or workspace root before reading or archiving files.

remediation.issue: Generated pages depend on external fonts and a CDN script.
remediation.suggestion: Self-host required assets or clearly disclose outbound requests. Add a restrictive content security policy for generated review pages.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Skill Content Can Inject Optimizer Prompt
semantic_findings.description: Skill content and failed eval queries are interpolated into a Claude CLI prompt without defensive isolation. Crafted content can redirect the optimizer and induce unintended agent actions.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code directly embeds skill_content and query text into the instruction prompt, then sends it to Claude. No untrusted-data policy or tool restriction is applied.

semantic_findings.title: Raw Eval Data Can Break Out of Script Context
semantic_findings.description: The review template places replacement JSON directly inside a script element. A query containing a closing script tag can inject JavaScript when the generated file opens.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The template expects raw JSON replacement in executable script context, and the workflow explicitly performs that replacement without escaping closing script sequences.

semantic_findings.title: Embedded Viewer Data Can Execute Script
semantic_findings.description: Workspace output and feedback data are serialized directly into a script element. A closing script sequence in embedded text can execute JavaScript in the review page.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: json.dumps does not escape the HTML closing script sequence, and the serialized value is inserted directly into executable script source.

semantic_findings.title: Packaging Follows Symlinks Outside Skill Root
semantic_findings.description: The packager treats symlinks to files as regular files and writes their target bytes into the archive. A crafted skill can include local files outside its directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_file follows symlinks, and ZipFile.write reads the resolved target. The loop does not reject symlinks or verify each resolved file remains under skill_path.

semantic_findings.title: Viewer Discovery Can Follow Workspace Symlinks
semantic_findings.description: Run discovery and output collection follow directory and file symlinks. A crafted workspace can embed local files outside the selected workspace into generated review HTML.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Path.is_dir and Path.is_file follow symlinks by default, and collected files are read and embedded. No resolved-path containment check is present.

content.value_statement: Creating reliable AI skills requires clear instructions, realistic tests, and measured iteration. This skill guides drafting, benchmarking, review, description optimization, and packaging.
actual_capabilities: Drafts new SKILL.md instructions from user goals, examples, constraints, and expected outputs.
Revises existing skills using human feedback, transcripts, benchmark results, and repeated test runs.
Creates realistic trigger and non-trigger queries for description evaluation.
Runs comparative evaluations with skill-enabled and baseline configurations when subagents are available.
Aggregates grades, timing, tokens, and review feedback into benchmark and HTML reports.
Optimizes skill descriptions with Claude CLI evaluations and packages validated skill directories.
limitations: Description optimization requires the Claude CLI, compatible authentication, and a selected model.
Rigorous baseline comparisons require subagents; single-agent environments provide weaker evidence.
Browser review may fail in headless environments, although static HTML output is available.
Automated grades and trigger scores do not replace human review of quality and safety.

use_cases.title: Create a New Skill
use_cases.description: Turn a repeated workflow into structured instructions, resources, tests, and a distributable skill package.

use_cases.title: Improve an Existing Skill
use_cases.description: Use user feedback and evaluation results to revise instructions and verify that changes improve outcomes.

use_cases.title: Compare Skill Versions
use_cases.description: Run baseline and updated versions, aggregate metrics, and review outputs before selecting the stronger version.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a skill for [workflow]. Ask essential questions, draft SKILL.md, and propose three realistic test prompts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a skill from a clear workflow idea.

prompt_templates.title: Revise an Existing Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the skill at [path]. Identify instruction gaps, preserve its name, revise the content, and explain each important change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a skill without running a full benchmark.

prompt_templates.title: Benchmark a Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate the skill at [path] using [test prompts]. Compare skill and baseline outputs, grade assertions, and generate a review report.
prompt_templates.scenario: Measure whether a skill improves task results.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Triggering
prompt_templates.prompt: Create balanced trigger tests for the skill at [path]. Review them with me, run description optimization, and apply the best held-out result.

output_examples.input: Create a skill for reviewing database migrations.
output: A focused skill draft with trigger guidance and a migration review workflow.
Three test prompts covering safe changes, risky changes, and irrelevant requests.
A proposed evaluation plan with human and automated checks.

output_examples.input: Improve my documentation skill using these review notes.
output_examples.output: A revised skill that generalizes the feedback, removes weak instructions, preserves the original name, and lists the main changes.

output_examples.input: Is version two better than version one?
output: A blind comparison of representative outputs.
Pass-rate, timing, and token summaries for both versions.
A recommendation grounded in observed quality and evaluation variance.

best_practices: Use realistic prompts that represent actual user language, files, constraints, and edge cases.
Combine automated assertions with human review before deciding that a revision is better.
Keep held-out tests separate from description improvement to reduce overfitting.
anti_patterns: Do not optimize only for a small set of easy or repetitive test prompts.
Do not replace subjective human judgment with pass rates alone.
Do not package or publish a skill before reviewing its scripts, permissions, and generated files.

faq.question: Can this create a skill from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It gathers requirements, drafts instructions, proposes tests, supports iteration, and can package the finished skill.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It can preserve the current name, revise instructions, compare versions, and apply feedback.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex?
faq.answer: Core drafting, review, and packaging workflows can work with Codex. Claude CLI description optimization remains Claude-specific.

faq.question: Are subagents required?
faq.answer: No. They improve parallel evaluation and baseline rigor, but simpler single-agent review remains possible.

faq.question: What files does it generate?
faq.answer: It can generate skill instructions, evaluation data, grading results, benchmarks, review pages, feedback files, and packaged skill archives.

faq.question: Does a high benchmark score guarantee quality?
faq.answer: No. Scores depend on test design and assertions. Human review remains necessary for usefulness, safety, and generalization.
